### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**3** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `VALIDATION_FAILED (literal, 50 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **19** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7878cf0557737ecfde78dfa9cff7a1046a289a4a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d9e6d20f4a8e07a7f6fa9b4ab0f52c41151bc992` — the merge of head `d6b03538fc4843e560c83ded2038f5c9fd938bc2` into base `7878cf0557737ecfde78dfa9cff7a1046a289a4a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d9e6d20f4a8e07a7f6fa9b4ab0f52c41151bc992 && git checkout d9e6d20f4a8e07a7f6fa9b4ab0f52c41151bc992
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7878cf0557737ecfde78dfa9cff7a1046a289a4a d6b03538fc4843e560c83ded2038f5c9fd938bc2 && git checkout -B drift-repro 7878cf0557737ecfde78dfa9cff7a1046a289a4a && git merge --no-ff d6b03538fc4843e560c83ded2038f5c9fd938bc2

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7878cf0557737ecfde78dfa9cff7a1046a289a4a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## 维护者速读
- 相关子表一次选多条添加、其中一条被服务器拒绝时，提示现在会写出是哪一条（用选择框里显示的名称），后面跟服务器给的原因。
- 服务器的批量接口在拒绝时多带一个字段，说明是第几个操作、哪个对象出的错；成功时的返回不变，仍然全成或全不成。
- 整批一起被拒的情况（例如对象级的权限或请求本身有问题）不指向某一条，提示保持原样。
- 这是接口上的一处只增不减的变化，需要席位做一次接口层面的复核后再合并。
- 席位意见：通过；转席位做接口复核，复核通过后分区转为正式再合并。

## 席位核对
**ACCEPT** · head `d6b03538fc` · Fixes #35726 (under #35601, seat ruling 07:43Z) · K=11 · merge-tree vs `origin/main` clean · governed: no · +272/−12, 7 files · CI 56 success, 12 skipped; the one failure is `PR-body guards` run 136196481799 (09:16:48Z), superseded by a success of the same check, 136199328673 (09:22:22Z) · draft · 2026-11-20T09:41Z

Routing: **`Clause-②: yes (widening)`** (the REST refusal body gains an optional key) → **L2 at CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER by the seat**, then the area lands it.

Checked:
- Server: `failedOperation` is set at the top of each op inside `runOps` and cleared once every op ran, so a commit-time failure names no op; the engine's up-front no-rollback 501 is raised before `runOps` and names none either. The blank-id refusal names its index directly. Object-level gates (exposure, API-key rule) and request-level refusals carry none, as the JSDoc says. The ⛔ rulings at ~463 (#14147 C) and ~495 (A-prime) are untouched; only the `failedOperation =` line lands beside the loop head.
- `namingFailedOperation`: wraps only `status()` and `json()` and adds the key to an object body; `handleRouteError` calls exactly `res.status(s).json(body)` (`error-response.ts`), so the status, code and sentence stay the door's. Absent an op, it returns `res` itself.
- No disclosure: `index` and `object` are the caller's own request's; the refusal sentence is unchanged, so a not-found or permission refusal reveals nothing it did not before.
- Client: the console adapter rethrows the SDK error as is on a declared atomic backend, so `err.details.failedOperation` reaches `handleAddRecords`. `opPicks` is pushed only beside an op (after the `pickedId == null` skip), so the indices line up; the label is the picker's display field, else the id; no index → the reason alone, as before.
- Surface: all 7 files inside claim 7035582958. The spec declares only the batch SUCCESS body (`CrossObjectBatchResponseSchema`); no refusal envelope is declared anywhere, so the claim's "if one exists" leaves nothing to edit.

For the L2 (ux-2's two questions):
- (1) Declare the refusal envelope in `packages/spec`: I agree with **A, no**. No other refusal detail on this route is declared, and declaring one key alone would make a partial contract.
- (2) The 409 package-scoped path: I agree with **A, accept**. It refuses the batch as a whole and has no per-op cause. Note that if a 409 is raised from inside an op, the wrapper will still add the index, which is correct.

Required before landing:
- **R1.** L2 by the seat, then mark the PR ready.

No other item.

## Seat contract note — PASS · head `d6b03538fc4843e560c83ded2038f5c9fd938bc2` · 2026-11-20T09:43Z

- **Face:** reviewFace finds no contract face on this file list (no `packages/spec`), so no isolated L2 record is owed. The seat read the `Clause-②: yes (widening)` itself because the REST refusal body gains a key.
- **The widening:** `failedOperation: { index, object }` is added to a refused cross-object batch's body only when one op is the cause. `index` and `object` echo the caller's own request, so they disclose nothing the caller did not send. The success body and the all-or-none outcome are unchanged (ADR-0119 D4). The changeset says when the key is present and when it is absent, and that matches the code: it is set per op inside the transaction, cleared after the last op, and stamped up front on the no-row refusal.
- **Mechanism:** `namingFailedOperation` wraps `res` only for `status().json()`, which is the only way `handleRouteError` writes (`error-response.ts`), so nothing else on `res` is shadowed.
- **Rulings:** (1) A: the envelope stays undeclared in `packages/spec`, since no other refusal detail on this route is declared and declaring one key alone would make a partial contract. (2) A: the package-scoped `409` refuses the batch as a whole and names no record.
- **Landing:** not governed, under 3,000 lines, K = 11, L1-a ACCEPT 7036225777. The owning area (ux-2) lands it.
